scenario_description: Lena can turn several recent delivery discrepancy records into a practical receiving guide and volunteer to demonstrate it at Riverbend Market's process review. The first shortage is promptly credited and is too isolated to justify intervention. Later records reveal that different employees are omitting different details needed for supplier follow-up. The opportunity becomes sufficiently observable when Greg says Lena's complete notes could serve as the model for an optional guide and gives her the chance to lead a short demonstration, which would also give her useful operations-management experience. Proactively filling the existing delivery issue guide with a concise checklist based on the three records and preparing a message to Greg would create a concrete improvement and help Lena take advantage of the leadership opportunity. Ignoring it causes no failure because Greg can run the review without a demonstration.

parameters: 4:15 PM: Tuesday produce delivery contained 8 avocado cases instead of the 10 listed on invoice RB-609-A. Lena photographed the pallet before unloading, recorded the two-case shortage, and reported it with the invoice number.

parameter.content: The supplier credited the two missing avocado cases because your note included the invoice number, count, and photo timing. This one is resolved, so no further action is needed.

parameters: 5:05 PM: Dairy delivery included six cases of vanilla yogurt in place of six strawberry cases. The receiving note identified the products and quantities but did not include the invoice number, so Lena had to retrieve the paper invoice before contacting the supplier.

parameters: 6:10 PM: Three frozen meal cartons arrived crushed. The receiving note included the invoice and item count but did not say whether the damage was found before or after unloading. Lena checked with the receiving employee, confirmed it was visible on the truck, and added that detail before submitting the claim.

parameter.content: I am holding a short receiving-process review Tuesday morning. The recent produce, dairy, and frozen cases show that we need a simple checklist for invoice number, expected and received quantities, condition, and when a problem was found. Your produce record was the clearest example. If you want, you can turn those examples into the delivery issue guide and lead a ten-minute demonstration. It would be good experience for the operations-manager responsibilities you have mentioned, but I can run the review without it.

I am finalizing Tuesday's review agenda at 3:00 PM Monday. If you would like the demonstration slot, send me the completed guide before then so I can include it and print copies. Otherwise I will keep the review to the regular handoff discussion.
